articles.standfirst: El técnico del Villarreal considera que la victoria cargará de moral a la plantilla
articles.summary: El técnico del Villarreal considera que la victoria cargará de moral a la plantilla
articles.body: Iñigo Pérez disfruta de su primera victoria con el Villarreal y reconoce que se han quitado una pesada mochila de encima. El técnico navarro destacó la capacidad de su equipo para sobreponerse tras el primer gol del Málaga. Mérito de sobreponerse: “Sí, hemos visto este partido alguna otra vez. Sobre todo el mérito es sobreponerse del primer gol viniendo de donde venimos y seguir jugando de la manera en la que han jugado. Partido redondo ante un rival muy complejo, estoy satisfecho". Sobre Moleiro: "Es el sistema habitual que utilizamos, independientemente del jugador que intervenga en la posición del 10, aunque por sus características parezca más 4-4-2. Creo que 'Mole', mi tendencia y pensamiento hacia él es que su puesto natural debe ser el de jugador número 10. También lo hace bien por fuera. Creo que era el momento de probar con él, ha estado bien y seguiremos explorando los nuevos espacios, pero yo creo que es una de las opciones que tenemos dentro de la plantilla". Golpe de moral: “Sí, y además hay que tener presente que se empezó perdiendo, que en esos momentos perfectamente podrían haber aparecido dudas, temor a que se repita una nueva derrota, este tipo de situaciones que pasan. Y ahora estoy muy contento, por la victoria y la manera de conseguirlo. La serenidad y fortaleza mental, han demostrado que pueden hacerlo. Es el momento de seguir analizando, corregir, digerirlo, disfrutar, saborear y ya veremos cómo reaccionamos". Lesión de Comesaña: “No he hablado con el árbitro sobre la cuestión de Santi. Fue un intercambio de opiniones. Si Santi abandona un campo por propia voluntad, es que tiene dolor, que tiene daño y veremos las pruebas que arrojan. Pero fue una pérdida para el partido importante, ojalá no sea mucho". Buenos rendimientos individuales: “Muchas veces no sabes cuándo va a suceder en un partido, cuándo se va a alinear el rendimiento individual, con el rendimiento colectivo, y a la postre con el resultado favorable. Hoy se han encontrado los tres rasgos, otras veces ha habido dos y no hemos conseguido la victoria, otras veces uno, a veces ninguno. Entonces, creo que es importante que el rendimiento individual, como nombras, podemos potenciarlo a nivel colectivo en Ayoze, en Ilias y en Mole, jugadores que tienen perfectamente esa altura y ese espacio del campo, que son difíciles de defender y, además, son jugadores muy comprometidos con el esfuerzo defensivo y la presión”. Discusión por lanzar el penalti: “Sobre las órdenes de los tiradores, la emoción y el contexto que se vive dentro no se vive fuera, por tanto, para dirigir ese tipo de situaciones muchas veces igual te falta información. He visto el típico intercambio de dos jugadores que quieren tirar el penalti para marcar. No creo que vaya a mayores, además tienen una excelente relación los dos”. Defensa de tres centrales al final: “ Sí, es un aspecto que creo que en el fútbol muchas veces se confunde. Ellos han metido doble delantero, cuando lo han hecho estábamos marcando al hombre, teníamos una ventaja de un gol y quizá era demasiado riesgo, por tanto, queríamos tener un tres contra dos en la última línea y muchas veces, sin hundirte, esa línea de 5 más 4 propicia errores del rival para tú poder transitar. No me importa que juguemos con muchos defensas, porque generalmente en los reducidos de los entrenamientos juegas defensas contra delanteros y acaban ganando los defensas. Es la forma, el modo, la intención de dónde defiendes, a qué altura... Estoy contento con ese momento, porque era delicado y habitualmente teníamos tendencia a defender el área demasiado atrás, hoy no ha sido así y las piezas son elegidas en función del momento del partido”. Cómo se siente: “A ver, hoy dormiré. La otra vez no, hoy sí dormiré. Sí, uno siente liberación por los jugadores, siente liberación por el presidente y su familia, que me tratan muy bien, se preocupan por mí, ven que, como ellos sufro, y entonces obtener esta victoria es muy bueno y liberador para todos. Me mantengo cauto, hemos hecho muchas cosas bien, hemos obtenido la victoria, pero también te diré que han alimentado un monstruo que es el de la exigencia, el perfeccionismo y si lo han hecho hoy, no les voy a dejar que bajen el nivel. Por lo menos, lo intentaremos mantener y ojalá cerremos esta primera parte de la temporada con una victoria en La Cerámica".

articles.title: Bournemouth: From -17 to dream European start for Adam Smith and Cherries
articles.summary: Bournemouth started a League Two season on -17 points in 2008, now they have made a dream start in European competition.
articles.body:
'From -17 to Europe', read a flag in the away end at at the Anoeta Stadium.

As Bournemouth embarked on the first European campaign in the club's 127-year history, it served as a reminder of just how far they have come.

But a 2-1 victory at Real Sociedad in their Europa League opener shows they are not ready to stop there.

It is now 11 years since the Cherries were first promoted to the Premier League, meaning there is now a generation of supporters who will view top-flight football as the norm.

From that perspective then, qualifying and playing in Europe might simply appear the next logical step for a well-run and ambitious club.

"It's a brilliant win in our first European game. It's brilliant for the club and the 2,000 fans from Bournemouth," manager Marco Rose told TNT Sports.

Yet for the vast majority of fans celebrating a famous victory on Thursday, the whole thing still seems surreal.

Just 18 years ago, the club was on the brink. A 10-point deduction for entering administration resulted in their relegation to League Two.

To even stay in the Football League for the 2008-09 season, they had to accept a 17-point deduction and agree not to appeal against the decision after it was ruled that, as they had been unable to agree a Company Voluntary Arrangement, they had not met their terms for exiting administration.

Thoughts of a £100m-rated midfielder picking out a Brazil winger to head Bournemouth to victory in Europe was the stuff of fantasy as the Dorset club battled for survival.

But that now is Bournemouth's reality with Alex Scott swaggering around San Sebastian, showing why there is such a clammer for his signature among top Premier League clubs, and Rayan providing another example of why the Cherries will demand every penny of a reported £130m release clause to let him go.

Bournemouth have nothing to compare it to but this was a proper European away performance.

Up against a Real Sociedad side led by a World Cup-winning forward in Mikel Oyarzabal and who beat Atletico Madrid to win the Copa del Rey last season, they were dominant for 45 minutes.

They suffocated Sociedad with their relentlessness off the ball, winning the ball back high up the pitch time and again and showing the quality on the ball to create chances - even when the defence was set.

But there is an edge to the Basque side and, poor as they had been, that they came out fighting after the break was no surprise.

The adrenaline-fueled exuberance of Rose's side in the first half appeared to catch up with them in the second, but their desire to compete never wavered.

Bournemouth are not known for their defensive resilience and, as Sociedad ramped up the pressure as the game wore on, thoughts might have turned to leads surrendered in each of their first four Premier League games.

But the Cherries, aided by the sharp reflexes of Djordje Petrovic in goal, held on to secure a famous win.

"It was very intense and tough," Rose told TNT Sports.

"Brilliant first half in everything. The way we won balls and the possession high up. In the second half, we needed to suffer because we were not so sharp."

Speaking on BBC Radio Solent, former Cherries full-back Charlie Daniels added: "It is a big occasion. A big moment for the club, and they should be applauded for it."

Bournemouth hold on to win at Sociedad on European bow

Cherries fans hail historic day in San Sebastian

Bournemouth's incredible rise can be traced back to the appointment of Eddie Howe in January 2009.

The former boss guided the Cherries to safety, finishing nine points clear of the relegation zone despite that 17-point deduction.

A mere six and a half years later, Howe - back for his second spell as manager - had taken a transformed Bournemouth to the Premier League.

It was fitting then, that on this latest milestone night for the club, the team was led out by a man involved during Howe's first stint.

Adam Smith joined Bournemouth on loan during the 2010-11 campaign, returned on a permanent deal in 2014 and has been at the club ever since, with approaching 400 league appearances to his name.

"Adam has been with the club for so long," Daniels said. "Dedicated himself to the club, and it's such a proud moment, not only for him, but for his family, his team-mates and old team-mates to see how he's grown - not only as a player but as a man as well.

"To lead out the Cherries on this historical night is fantastic."

Smith also made history of his own, becoming, at 35 years and 141 days, the oldest English outfielder to make their debut in major European competition since Ipswich's Reginald Pickett in 1962.

The club captain will appreciate more than most what a special night this was for Bournemouth.

Things have been far from straightforward for the club, even in recent years, with relegation in 2020 and, since re-establishing themselves in the top-flight, the seemingly annual battle to replace players picked off by Europe's top clubs.

Even qualifying for Europe was not enough to keep hold of manager Andoni Iraola, who returns to the Vitality Stadium with his new club Liverpool on Sunday.

That pattern is unlikely to stop anytime soon but, while there is the prospect of more nights like this one, Bournemouth supporters won't be complaining.

They've seen enough to know that these are the good times.

articles.title: Ole Miss Issues Warning About LSU Gear in Student Section Ahead of Lane Kiffin's Return
articles.summary: Ole Miss is taking steps to avoid any altercations during Saturday's game against Lane Kiffin and LSU.
articles.body:
Ole Miss is taking steps to avoid any altercations during Saturday's game against Lane Kiffin and LSU.

Insider Tyler Komis relayed a message Ole Miss sent to its students on Thursday that said, "No person wearing an opposing team's gear or colors will be allowed entrance into the student section.

"Additionally, anyone found to be wearing opposing team apparel or colors in the student section will be removed."

Belichick Shuts Down 'Ridiculous' GF Rumors

This comes after the Mississippi Department of Public Safety announced it will have an enhanced law enforcement presence on and around campus for Saturday's game.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry also joked about what he might need to do to protect Kiffin as the LSU head coach returns to his former school.

"I'm thinking about having to send him in on an F-16 and maybe the team on a C-130," he said, per ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "Security is going to be really tight. You know, we might need the National Guard out there to protect our team. I think it's going to be an interesting weekend."

For his part, Kiffin made sure his players knew all they have to worry about is playing.

"We talk about that," Kiffin said. "I guess there's real safety issues and stuff, so there's people that have a plan for that. I told the players today, 'Man, you don't have anything to worry about as far as, like, attention on you all week and everything. There's going to be so much attention, hatred, everything on me. You just get to go play.'"

It will surely be a heated environment on Saturday, as Kiffin coached the Rebels to the College Football Playoff last season.

However, he decided to take the LSU job before the CFP started in a coaching transition that generated plenty of attention. Kiffin wanted to remain at Ole Miss and coach the team during the postseason, but that ultimately didn't happen.

"Ole Miss doesn't want Kiffin around its players with the transfer portal opening on Jan. 2," ESPN's Schlabach and Pete Thamel reported at the time. "The Rebels also don't want their CFP games to be a 'commercial' for LSU's future under Kiffin."

John Talty of CBS Sports reported that some Ole Miss players even "confronted" Kiffin about attempting to take some of the assistant coaches with him to LSU, and the coach responded by saying, "I'm not making them go. They can do whatever they want."

As if all the attention on Kiffin wasn't enough, it is also a massive showdown with SEC and CFP implications.

LSU is No. 7 in the country, while Ole Miss is No. 8. Whichever team wins will have a marquee victory to add to its resume and move up in the conference rankings, which will surely only add to the overall atmosphere.

articles.title: Leaden, stale, disheartening - where do Celtic & Martin O'Neill go from here?
articles.summary: After another defeat, keeping the faith is surely becoming more testing for Celtic's fans, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
To Celtic fans it might seem like sacrilege to doubt Martin O'Neill's capacity to get them through whatever it is they're going through right now - a slump or something deeper - but keeping the faith is surely becoming testing.

After their shellacking at Ibrox on Sunday, Celtic's response against Ferencvaros was another heavy defeat and three more goals conceded.

More absent-minded stuff in the midfield, more loose defending, more negativity and lack of accuracy on the ball, no great grasp of the basics of pass and move, not enough intensity, not enough work-rate, not enough of anything that you need to give yourself a chance.

At times, as it meandered along at 3-1 to Ferencvaros, Celtic tried to stage some kind of gallop but their attempts were from distance, hopeful efforts rather than anything built on the back of coherence and pressing and speed.

Celtic at their best - in the finest days under Ange Postecoglou - were all about aggression and ingenuity, about dynamism and risk-taking, about pace and belief and pulling defenders into places where they did not want to be.

Fragile Celtic beaten by Ferencvaros in Europa League opener

Celtic are 'little bit broken' - but is change of shape 'worth risking'?

Reaction, analysis & have your say on Celtic's defeat

Things can turn quickly in Scottish football.

The second act of this season's Old Firm show on Sunday is still a hard one to call, partly because it's at Celtic Park and also because there surely has to be some kind of response from O'Neill's team to their pitiful fate at Ibrox last weekend.

Their fans will be worried, though. Five goals given up against LASK, a desperate experience at Ibrox - and now this.

In moments on Thursday, some of their football was reminiscent of darker days - the failures of Cluj and Copenhagen in 2019 and 2020, when Bayo and Bolingoli were in the building; Sparta Prague in 2020, when Klimala and Ajeti, Duffy and Laxalt were in the team.

It was all very Legia Warsaw, very Salzburg, very Maribor. The energy levels were low, the booing was loud and the feeling of a side with no answers was unmissable.

In the aftermath, O'Neill spoke about frustration, failure and psychological damage, how low moments like these hit you hard and test your resolve. He promised to "get ourselves together" for Rangers on Sunday but his tone was flat and a touch tired.

He outlined some of the ways in which Celtic were deficient on the night but didn't talk with the spirit of a man who had answers. In many ways his post-match comments mirrored his team's performance - leaden, stale, disheartening.

O'Neill has fixed many problems over the years, not just in his first trophy-laden spell but in his return to chaos last season. He restored order and confidence, two things that have been lost.

The force of his personality gave Celtic fight. They were not always pretty to watch but they were ferociously hard to beat. Nobody managed it on the title run-in.

That kind of never-say-die only seems like yesterday, but in other ways it feels like an awfully long time ago.

They had a decent start against Ferencvaros, then conceded a soft goal. They hauled themselves back into it with a little glimpse of quality, but then fell back into destructive ways. Safe passes, little zeal, only a modicum of fire and emotion.

The goal they conceded just before the break was the type of goal that poor sides give away. Hesitancy in the first instance to fight for the loose ball, weakness in the second instance when trying to prevent the cross and then defensive disorganisation and bewilderment in the end.

Celtic had 62.5% possession in the opening half but trailed 2-1. Camilo Duran, playing through the middle ahead of Kasper Hogh, had eight touches of the ball.

Duran was in his favoured position but offered little. A player who showed such zest and love of his new life in Glasgow only a few short weeks ago is looking a shadow of himself.

Hogh, with goals against Man City (two), Atletico Madrid, Inter Milan, Sporting, Porto, Jagiellonia and Olympiacos (three) for Bodo Glimt, has morphed into an awkward looking centre-forward with a poor first touch and no chances to feed on.

He has now scored in just one of his eight games as a Celtic player. O'Neill has so far failed to get the best out of a player the club paid £11m for.

Callum McGregor, the great totem, is looking a little lost. O'Neill has all the nous in the world to arrest this, but he needs to do it quickly. It has to be said, he doesn't look or sound all that convincing.

The way things are going for Celtic you could almost have guaranteed a goal for Daniel Arzani, their former player who came and went in a blur of nothingness.

To add salt, it was a magnificent strike after a counter-attack that exposed Celtic in the most embarrassing way. There was more order in the Keystone Cops.

Arzani appeared in acres of space on the left, Colby Donovan having over-committed to attack and now busting a gut in a forlorn attempt to recover. Arzani had patience and precision. He whipped his shot into the top corner. Easy.

O'Neill needs some amount of solutions in the coming days. Football is weird. He might find them, but his team is lacking ideas, conviction, composure, physical and psychological heft, creativity, ruthlessness and stomach for a fight.

The manager, himself, looks like he's lacking in any inspiration. He's bounced back from challenging situations in his football past and you almost become attuned to him doing so again, but there is a lot to fix here.

McGregor says the team is a little bit broken at the moment. Rangers might be licking their lips at the prospect of facing a wounded animal. Beware the backlash and all of that, but they have an opportunity to land another blow.

Sunday will tell us much about the way of things between the Glasgow giants.

McGregor says the team is a little bit broken at the moment. Rangers might be licking their lips at the prospect of facing a wounded animal. Beware the backlash and all of that, but they have an opportunity to land another blow.

Sunday will tell us much about the way of things between the Glasgow giants.

articles.summary: Welcome back, readers!
articles.body:
Welcome back, readers! I am happy to return for a second year as The Sporting Tribune's fantasy football analyst. If you are new here, my mission is to help fantasy managers with any dilemmas or questions they may have through the course of the season to ultimately win their leagues. For the next 17 weeks, I will produce weekly fantasy content that will go over the waiver wire, rankings, and Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns.

Being a fantasy manager often means having to make difficult roster decisions, but I aim to take some of the guesswork out of it with my Start 'Em and Sit 'Em column for every position. It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride " or "sit Tommy DeVito ." Instead, I search for players that could be perceived as fringe that could propel your lineups for weekly wins.

As always, if you have any questions or don't see your players on here, feel free to follow me on Twitter (X) – @JamesNewell96 and send me a message, where I typically respond in a timely manner.

Eagles Defense @ TEN (Projected FPTS – 8.3): The Eagles have a cupcake of a matchup this week against Cam Ward and a Titans offense that has struggled so far. Tennessee scored just 10 points and put up only 195 yards of total offense, while their O-line gave up three sacks. The Eagles' defense should have a field day on Sunday.

Buccaneers Defense vs. CLE (Projected FPTS – 8.2): The Buccaneers also have a fantastic matchup this week against a poorly run Browns offense that will have Deshaun Watson under center. Behind a shaky O-line, Watson was sacked five times, and the offense coughed up two turnovers. The Bucs should finish in the top three in fantasy points scored by a defense in Week Two.

49ers Defense vs. MIA (Projected FPTS – 8.2): The 49ers impressed a lot of people with their performance against the Rams last week. With a healthy Nick Bosa and Fred Warner , San Francisco held Matthew Stafford and company to just seven points and forced two takeaways. In Week Two, they'll square off against the Dolphins, who allowed the Raiders' defense to finish with 14 fantasy points. I'd expect the Niners' defense to finish with the highest fantasy point total this week.

Honorable Mentions: Chargers Defense vs. LV; Ravens Defense vs. NO; Seahawks Defense @ ARI; Panthers Defense @ ATL

Vikings Defense vs. CHI (Projected FPTS – 6.1): Despite pulling off a crazy comeback against the Packers last week, the Vikings' defense allowed Jordan Love to have a great day on the stat sheet. Now they'll take on the potential best offense in the league — Chicago 's offense scored 59 points and finished with 552 yards of total offense in its win over the Panthers. Avoid Minnesota this week.

Broncos Defense vs. JAX (Projected FPTS – 6.5): The Broncos' defense was a huge letdown last week in their loss to the Chiefs , surrendering 31 points and nearly 400 yards of total offense. In Week Two, they have Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars offense on deck, who have been scorching opposing defenses since last season. Even with the home crowd behind them, I don't like the matchup and would look elsewhere this week.

Lions Defense @ BUF (Projected FPTS – 5.4): The Lions nearly let the Saints complete a 21-0 comeback victory in the second half. They finished with five fantasy points last week and will now face the Bills in the debut of their new stadium. Josh Allen and company are coming off an electric performance against the Texans in Houston , and if they could run over that defense, they'll do it to anybody else. Whatever you do, DO NOT START DETROIT!

Lowlights: Rams Defense vs. NYG; Texans Defense vs. CIN; Jaguars Defense @ DEN; Bills Defense vs. DET.

articles.title: Juventus, Palace cruise to Europa League wins, Bournemouth beat Sociedad
articles.summary: Juventus began their quest for Europa League glory with a 5-0 thrashing of NEC Nijmegen, while Bournemouth secured an impressive victory at Real Sociedad on...
articles.body:
Juventus began their quest for Europa League glory with a 5-0 thrashing of NEC Nijmegen, while Bournemouth secured an impressive victory at Real Sociedad on their European debut on Thursday.

Crystal Palace were 4-0 winners over Lech Poznan, but Celtic suffered another European embarassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros.

Juventus expect to be competing among Europe's elite in the Champions League, but the failure to qualify last season has at least allowed them the chance to end a 30-year wait for a continental trophy.

The Italian giants were far too strong for their Dutch visitors in Turin as Nico Gonzalez, Kerim Alajbegovic and Nick Woltemade , with his first goal since joining on loan from Newcastle, made it 3-0 before half-time.

Zeki Celik and Randal Kolo Muani rounded off the scoring after the break as Juventus made a better start than rivals AC Milan , who lost 2-0 to Benfica in the pick of Wednesday's Europa League action.

Bournemouth had a dream start to their first ever European adventure with a 2-1 win in San Sebastian.

Justin Kluivert opened the scoring before Rayan headed in at the back post to put the Cherries 2-0 up inside 20 minutes.

Blowing leads has been a repeat occurence for Marco Rose's team in the early weeks of the season.

Rose is yet to taste victory in the Premier League despite Bournemouth going ahead in all four matches so far this season.

"It's a brilliant win in our first European game," said Rose. "It's brilliant for the club and the 2,000 fans from Bournemouth."

Sergio Gomez 's attempted cross flew into the far corner to bring Sociedad back into the contest, but this time Bournemouth held on for a memorable victory.

Conference League winners last season, Palace proved far too strong for Lech Poznan to complete a clean sweep of eight victories for the English sides in Champions and Europa League action so far this season.

Yeremy Pino pounced on a calamitous Poznan throw-in to open the scoring at Selhurst Park.

Chris Richards added a second before Jørgen Strand Larsen's penalty made it 3-0 and Eddie Nketiah rounded off the scoring.

Just weeks on from crashing out of the Champions League qualifiers to Austrian side LASK, despite at one point holding a four-goal lead, Celtic's defensive flaws were exposed once more.

Martin O'Neill's side also suffered a chastening 3-0 defeat to local rivals Rangers last weekend and failed to deliver on their manager's promise to respond.

"It's a huge frustration, obviously, but it's also psychologically quite damning as well," said O'Neill.

"Tonight was I think a European lesson for us in many aspects."

Daniel Arzani 's sensational strike on his return to Celtic Park capped a fine night for Ferencvaros after a Liam Scales own goal and Kristoffer Zachariassen put the visitors in front.

Besiktas inflicted a fourth consecutive defeat on Marseille with a 4-1 win in Istanbul.

Vaclav Cerny, Micahel Amir Murillo and Ernest Poku struck in the second half after Keyliane Abdallah had cancelled out Ilhan Fakili's opener for the Turkish side.

articles.title: Ole Miss bans LSU gear and colors from student section for Saturday's clash, Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford
articles.summary: Additionally, the area where visiting team buses arrive at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium will be fenced off for Saturday's game.
articles.body:
Is Ole Miss being proactive or overreactive before Saturday's widely anticipated matchup with LSU and the return of head coach Lane Kiffin to Oxford?

The reception by Rebels fans toward their former coach who spurned them before the end of last season presents an intriguing backdrop for a game that was already meaningful with the Nos. 7 and 8 teams in this week's AP Top 25 facing each other.

Fearing any possible incidents among fans or outbursts directed at Kiffin and the LSU team, Ole Miss is taking steps to prevent anything untoward. On Thursday, the school announced that fans would not be allowed to wear the "opposing team's gear or colors" in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium for Saturday's game.

"Effective immediately, no person wearing an opposing team's gear or colors will be allowed entrance into the student section," read a statement sent to students by the Ole Miss athletic department ( via Tyler Komis on X ). "Additionally, anyone found to be wearing opposing team apparel or colors in the student section will be removed."

"Effective immediately, no person wearing an opposing team's gear or colors will be allowed entrance into the student section," read a statement sent to students by the Ole Miss athletic department ( via Tyler Komis on X ).

"Additionally, anyone found to be wearing opposing team apparel or colors in the student section will be removed."

Another measure Ole Miss has taken is building a fence around the area where the visiting team buses arrive at the stadium on gameday, according to On3's Pete Nakos .

These two initiatives follow Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry joking that extraordinary measures could be taken to protect Kiffin and the LSU team during their trip to Oxford.

"I'm thinking about having to send him in on an F-16 and maybe the team on a C-130," Landry told ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "Security is going to be really tight. You know, we might need the National Guard out there to protect our team. I think it's going to be an interesting weekend."

Landry added that his office has talked to Ole Miss officials about ensuring proper security for the LSU contingent. He expressed his hope that "Southern hospitality" would prevail in the stadium on Saturday night.

In yet another proactive step, the Mississippi Department of Public Safety announced that "an enhanced law enforcement presence" would be in Oxford for Saturday's game. That will incude the largest deployment of the Mississippi Highway Patrol ever used for a college football game, according to MDPS commissioner Sean Tindell.

"This weekend will bring a significant number of visitors to Oxford, and our priority is making sure everyone can enjoy the game and surrounding events safely," Tindell said in a statement . "This enhanced presence is about being prepared, staying proactive, and working together."

Perhaps previewing what Mississippi and school authorities are attempting to prevent, tensions flared up in April at a baseball game in Oxford between Ole Miss students and an LSU fan during which punches were thrown, according to the Clarion Ledger .

ESPN's "College GameDay" will broadcast from Oxford on Saturday morning with actor Morgan Freeman (an Ole Miss fan) selected as the show's guest picker. Kickoff for LSU at Ole Miss is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday night and will be televised on ABC.
